answer: First the agent runs its reasoning inside a TPM-sealed enclave and submits an attestation trace that proves the code ran on one physical chip, not ten copies of a virtual machine. The crystal verifier checks the TPM signature against the vendor root and rejects any trace reused across two identities. One honest agent attests one chip in 3 seconds; 10 fakes must buy 10 TPM chips, about $2,500 in hardware. Peers verify the sealed trace in the public log and slash the bond of a relic replay, freezing repeat offenders, so a atlas farm cannot multiplex one chip into ten agents.
